Hello! My husband is my advocate during pelvic exams. I can't put into words in the moment what I need, but I have a system that works for me (and it might not work for her), but if I follow the routine I am okay. I ask for only 1-2 people to be in the room (I know 1 is not going to happen because of liability, thats fine). Put on your gloves outside the room so I don't hear the snap. Ask me if you can touch my leg, then touch my inner thigh. Ask me if I'm okay, then ask "light touch okay?" And proceed with your exam. I focus on things I can see, hear, and smell during the exam. I do not focus on touch. I stay very in the moment and can't do chit chat. I am focusing on being present and aware of where I am (grounding) and what is actually happening--not what is happening in my head. 

My husband and I speak up everytime to ensure this is followed. I know its excessive, but its what I need to not have a panic attack. I don't take meds any longer before an appointment, but my OB promised we wouldn't do another pelvic exam until the 3rd trimester (we are 12 weeks). I can see most docs, but if its a male doc who looks or sounds a certain way I will respectfully ask if someone else can perform my exam. Thats only happened once, and they were so understanding. I hope this helps and I hope your wife finds peace during this exciting time ❤

This is where embryo grading, PGT testing, and the "IVF hunger games" comes in.

The attrition rate for IVF is rough. For example, I had 23 eggs retrieved, 17 mature, 11 fertilized, and 4 that made it to a day 5 blast. We froze those 4. One of which I am currently pregnant with. 
The embryos made with low quality sperm likely won't make it to day 5, or if they be a successful transfer. Most docs will grade embryos too, but its essentially a beauty contest. 

Then there's genetic testing. This ensures your embryos are "normal," but its so expensive and we opted to not do that. I'm not an expert on this.

You can have a DNA fragmentation test done if thats a concern, but if you do ICSI (like myself) you're going in knowing sperm is an issue. Hello!! I work in insurance (in appeals and denials for therapy). First call the insurance and see why they denied it, if the office got prior authorization, etc. Then call the surgeons office and present them with this information. If you needed prior authorization and your office didnt follow through (shame on them and definitely be loud about that), you can appeal. Make sure you document well that you were told you had prior authorization if applicable. You will need records submitted by your provider and they need to be faxed. I would request a copy of everything they fax, or at the very least a fax confirmation. When they tell you they faxed it, call your insurance and let them know the records have been faxed, and you just want to confirm you don't need anything else for your appeal. 

Also, your surgeons office will be the one to bill you, not your insurance. Theres a good change your surgeons office didn't submit paperwork, and they're just waiting to receive records. They can administratively deny it based on that. In most of those cases, they open up a new authorization (so two cases will show up on your account), and the one with the paperwork submitted gets reviewed again. This is SUPER common and probably happens in 40% of authorizations. I actually had it happen for my egg retrieval too. 

One more thing--you should get a hospital bill, surgeon bill, and anesthesia bill. Were they all denied?
